KEY MESSAGE 1...Cool weather and periods of showers will continue 
today and tonight, with a line of showers and thunderstorms forming 
along and just ahead of a cold front as it crosses the region this 
afternoon.

Deepening mid and upper level trough will continue to dig from the 
central Great Lakes into the lower Great Lakes region today into 
tonight. In the process, the mid level circulation will close off as 
the system becomes vertically stacked. This will act to slow the 
systems' progression as it drifts slowly southeastward, eventually 
right over NYS later tonight. The associated surface low will drift 
slowly east, just to the north of Lake Ontario today, then southward 
across NYS later tonight.  

Showers will continue through mid to late morning ahead of a warm 
front and pre-frontal trough pushing through western and 
northcentral NY. Expect a brief lull in the more widespread shower 
activity around midday in the wake of the the two aforementioned 
features, before a line of showers and thunderstorms ignite along 
and ahead of a surface cold front crossing the region this 
afternoon. Expect the line of showers and storms to initially 
develop early this afternoon from around the Chautauqua Ridge/Boston 
Hills area extending northeast into Wyoming and Genesee counties, 
then progress east through the Genesee Valley/Finger Lakes region, 
and lastly into the eastern Lake Ontario region by the mid to late 
afternoon hours. Most of these areas will just experience general 
thunderstorms accompanied by brief downpours. PWAT values remain 
fairly modest, peaking at around 0.75" mitigating the threat of 
excessive rainfall/flood threat. That said, there will be a brief 
window for a few stronger storms this afternoon from the interior 
Southern Tier northeast into the Finger Lakes and southern Tug Hill 
regions. Some breaks in the clouds this afternoon will aid
diurnal heating, helping to boost instability/steepen low level 
lapse rates with CAPE values in the 500-1000 J/kg range. This 
combined with 30-40 knots of bulk shear may yield a few more 
robust storms capable of producing isolated strong to severe 
wind gusts. SPC continues with a Marginal Risk for these 
aforementioned areas. Otherwise, expect a west to east drying 
trend in the wake of the cold front through the afternoon into 
this evening for much of the area. However, the cold front is 
expected to stall out just east of the area tonight, keeping the
potential for a few shower going east of Lake Ontario through 
much of the overnight. Meanwhile, as the mid level and 
associated surface low slowly pivot southeast across NYS, cool 
moist W to NW flow on the back side of the system will combine 
with some limited lake enhancement to bring chances for showers 
back in across far western NY late tonight, especially across 
favored upslope areas.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Unsettled and very cool weather will continue 
Thursday through Thursday night.

A mid level closed low will gradually move southeast across NY/PA on 
Thursday. The associated surface low just north of Lake Ontario in 
the morning will dissipate, giving way to secondary coastal 
cyclogenesis near the New York Bight by Thursday afternoon. The 
conveyor of deep moisture with this system will be well east of the 
area over eastern NY and New England Thursday, leaving more shallow 
wrap around moisture over the eastern Great Lakes. Cool air aloft, 
steepening lapse rates, and increasing northwest upslope flow will 
support a few showers at times, with the best coverage likely found 
across the western Southern Tier and Lewis County. 

A few showers will continue Thursday night, with the best coverage 
east of Lake Ontario in closer proximity to Atlantic moisture 
advecting westward around the northern periphery of the vertically 
stacked low off the southern New England coast. Additional rainfall 
amounts Thursday through Thursday night will be light.

The next mid level shortwave will move into northwest Ontario 
province Friday, forcing the closed low off the New England coast to 
accelerate eastward and out to sea. Rain chances will end from west 
to east for most of the area early in the morning, although a few 
showers may linger through the day east of Lake Ontario. 

Temperatures will be unseasonably cool Thursday, with highs only in 
the low to mid 50s for lower elevations and upper 40s for higher 
terrain, close to 15 degrees below average. Lows Thursday night will 
drop back into the low to mid 40s areawide.

KEY MESSAGE 3...A notable warming trend will start Friday, then gain 
momentum over the weekend with summer-like heat by early next week.

The very cool temperatures Thursday will give way to the start of a 
warming trend by Friday as the mid level low moves away, with some 
sunshine and weak warm advection beginning. Highs will recover into 
the 60s and close to average by Friday afternoon.
